jobs.occupation: Research Data Management & Digital Infrastructure Officer
jobs.description:
Can you combine technical understanding, stakeholder management, and practical execution to advance research data and IT initiatives across a complex organization?

  The Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH) is one of Europe's leading health faculties and home to the recently established Center for Core Facilities (CCF), which brings together world-class research infrastructures to support excellence in research, innovation, and education. 

  To further strengthen CCF's digital capabilities, we are seeking a proactive and solutions-oriented Research Data Management & Digital Infrastructure Officer to co-design and implement a data management and digital infrastructure framework across the Center. Working closely with the University of Copenhagen IT Department (UCPH-IT) and data experts from CCF's core facilities, the successful candidate will help develop sustainable solutions that support cutting-edge research and technology platforms.

  About the Role - The role combines research data management, stakeholder coordination, and IT technical expertise to ensure that users generating data at CCF's research infrastructures have access to data services to optimally collect, annotate, store and FAIR share AI-ready quality data.

  The successful candidate will become part of a highly international and interdisciplinary center, working closely with technology and data experts at CCF, UCPH-IT, and national and international key stakeholders to create a multi-technology data infrastructure and management ecosystem towards quality AI-ready data. 

  As leading force of the CCF Data Infrastructure Working Group, the successful candidate will have the following Key Responsibilities:

   	
• Drive the design and implementation of a CCF research data infrastructure, with particular focus on efficient and optimal data processing, analysis, storage and file systems. 	
• Lead and support research data management activities, including FAIRification of data practices and data lifecycle management. 	
• Maintain oversight of CCF data assets, including ownership, retention, storage, and deletion processes. 	
• Serve as the primary interface between CCF Core Facilities and external stakeholders (incl. UCPH-IT, DeiC, ELIXIR, EOSC and others), ensuring effective operation of CCF data infrastructure. 	
• Advise on data security, data governance, and compliance with institutional policies and relevant regulations. 	
• Identify, implement, and improve tools and workflows that support, improve and optimize CCF research data management. 	
• Track ongoing initiatives, maintain institutional knowledge, and help drive projects to completion.   We are looking for a person that has:

   	
• Experience with research data management and FAIR data principles. 	
• Strong understanding of IT infrastructure, particularly computing and storage systems and file management. 	
• Familiarity with GDPR, institutional data policies, and large-scale IT projects is an advantage. 	
• Experience coordinating complex projects involving multiple stakeholders. 	
• Ability to translate researchers' needs into technical requirements and vice versa. 	
• Knowledge of information security and data governance. 	
• Experience working with research environments is highly desirable. 	
• Fluent English is a must, and Danish is an asset.   We are looking for a candidate who is:

   	
• Proactive, persistent, and able to drive initiatives forward. 	
• Comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders and advocating for researchers' needs. 	
• Willing to challenge the status quo and propose new solutions. 	
• Equally capable of strategic thinking and hands-on implementation. 	
• An effective communicator who can build bridges between researchers and IT professionals. 	
• Organized, collaborative, and focused on achieving practical outcomes.   Terms of salary and employment
 The successful candidate will join the CCF Administration and Development team, To start with, the employment is a full-time one-year term position, as it is linked to a pilot grant. However, our vision is to work with the successful candidate to create a financial model to sustain data services beyond the grant period. 

  Employment will be as a special consultant in accordance with the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and academics in the state (the AC collective agreement). It is possible to negotiate supplements according to qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

  Application
 Send your application with your CV and relevant documentation via the Job Portal (click on "APPLY FOR THE POSITION" at the bottom of the advertisement) so that it is received by us no later than 22 December 2026. 

  Further information
 Questions regarding the position may be directed to CCF Director, Clara Prats, at cprats@sund.ku.dk.

  We want to represent the surrounding society and encourage everyone, regardless of background, to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Integrated Sustainability Screening for Early-Stage Technology Development under Uncertainty - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
The Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering of the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has an open PhD position on the topic of “Integrated Sustainability Screening for Early-Stage Technology Development under Uncertainty”. 

The position is in the context of the project Turbo Impact - TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology, a new Marie Skłodowska Curie (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme funded by the European Commission, that brings together 6 universities and 12 industry partners from 9 countries. Find more information at https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350.

Turbo Impact trains a new generation of creative and innovative manufacturing and materials researchers, with strong analytical, computational, and experimental skills and a deep understanding of all aspects of producing metallic, ceramic and multi-material small scale turbomachinery components and systems. In the framework of the doctoral network, the PhD student will work closely with a cohort of 14 PhD students working on different but related topics within the domain of turbomachinery components design and manufacturing.

General and project specific eligibility requirements
All applicants must fulfil the following general eligibility criteria, or otherwise will be rejected:

• must have completed a Master's degree or equivalent at the time of start
• must not have a doctoral degree at the date of their recruitment
• must comply with the mobility rules, where they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organization for more than 12 months, at any point during the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date (short stays such as holidays or compulsory military service are not taken into account).
Essential language requirements
The working language of Turbo Impact is English.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD position is hosted by DTU Construct's Section for Design for Sustainability and closely affiliated with the DTU Centre for Absolute Sustainability. The research focuses on the development and validation of methods, tools, and decision-support frameworks for integrating sustainability considerations into early-stage technology and product development under conditions of uncertainty.

The project aims to develop robust sustainability screening approaches that enable engineers and decision-makers to evaluate environmental, economic, and technical performance when data availability is limited and design freedom is high. Particular emphasis will be placed on combining relative and absolute sustainability perspectives, uncertainty analysis, and trade-off assessment to support sustainability-oriented innovation and technology development within advanced manufacturing and turbomachinery systems.

Key research activities include:

• Development of robust sustainability screening approaches for early-stage technology and product development.
• Development of methods for integrating uncertainty analysis and incomplete data into sustainability assessment and engineering decision-making.
• Development of approaches for translating sustainability assessment results into actionable design and development decisions.
• Development of guidelines and decision-support tools for embedding sustainability considerations into engineering design workflows.
The project will utilise a combination of industrial case studies, abridged sustainability screening methods, modelling approaches, and experimental data generated within the consortium to develop and validate practical decision-support frameworks. Validation will be conducted in collaboration with industrial and academic partners across the turbomachinery value chain.

The position involves both theoretical and applied research, with responsibilities spanning methodology development, industrial collaboration, and academic dissemination. The candidate will be expected to:

• Position the scientific work within the context of current literature in sustainability screening, engineering design, and decision-making under uncertainty.
• Collaborate with academic and industrial partners through workshops, case studies, and co-development activities.
• Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and present results at international conferences.
• Contribute to teaching, supervision, and student activities within the Section for Design for Sustainability and the Centre for Absolute Sustainability.
We are looking for candidates with:

• An excellent academic background in engineering design, sustainability engineering, industrial ecology, industrial engineering, environmental engineering, mechanical engineering, or related fields.
• Strong interest in sustainability-oriented technology development and engineering decision-making.
• Knowledge of sustainability screening and assessment methods, product development processes, and engineering systems.
• Experience with quantitative modelling, data analysis, and programming tools such as MATLAB or Python.
• Familiarity with uncertainty analysis, life cycle assessment, multicriteria decision analysis, systems thinking, or related approaches is a strong asset.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in interdisciplinary teams.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
You should have completed a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) in Engineering Design, Sustainability Engineering, Industrial Ecology, Industrial Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related discipline, or a similar degree with an equivalent academic level. 

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Demand Estimation for Large-Scale Transport Networks using Travel Surveys and 5G Data - DTU Management
jobs.description:
Are you passionate about data analytics, optimization, transport, and environment? Do you want to work on a research project that has a concrete impact on society? 

We invite you to apply for a full-time PhD position at DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) as part of an international Alliance PhD collaboration between DTU Management and Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IPP), France. The project “ASTRA” (Analytics for Spatio-Temporal Regional trAnsport models) explores how emerging data sources can be better integrated into demand estimation, and aims to develop a working prototype for the national Danish transport model.

Knowing how many people travel, where and when is the foundation of every transport model, and ultimately of decisions on infrastructure investments, transport policy and the green transition. Yet estimating mobility demand for large networks remains one of the main bottlenecks in transport modelling. The problem is highly non-linear, underdetermined and difficult to solve for large-scale networks, and existing methods often rely on proprietary, non-reproducible data and an oversimplified representation of travel behaviour. As a result, they often fail to represent travel decisions realistically, which can lead to misallocated infrastructure and ineffective policy interventions. At the same time, new data sources are emerging. Mobile networks, and in particular 5G antennas, continuously capture anonymous mobility traces, while travel surveys provide rich behavioural and socio-economic information, but only for small samples, and are rarely used in demand estimation.

The ASTRA project will develop a demand estimation framework that combines high-resolution behavioural data, such as the Danish National Travel Survey, with large-scale, low-resolution data, such as traffic counts and mobile phone network data. The aim is to realistically capture behaviour while remaining applicable to national-scale networks. A key expected outcome of the project is a demand estimation model for the Danish national transport model, the Green Mobility Model (GMM). Collaboration with the Danish Road Directorate (Vejdirektoratet) is therefore anticipated, to ensure real-life deployment.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The overall focus of this project is to develop scalable, behaviourally realistic methods for estimating travel demand on national-scale transport networks. You are expected to work closely with a PhD student at IPP and with the Danish Road Directorate. Your primary tasks will be to:

• Investigate how 5G network data can reveal recurrent demand patterns in space and time.
• Analyse and extract behavioural information from the Danish National Travel Survey.
• Develop a consistent data-integration and scaling pipeline to combine survey data, traffic counts, and mobile phone network data.
• Extend traditional demand estimation frameworks so that they can capture departure time, trip purpose and spatio-temporal flexibility.
• Build and validate a demand estimation model for the Green Mobility Model.
• Publish and present your results in international journals and conferences.
• Carry out research stays at IPP in Paris.
The project sits at the intersection of transport modelling and telecommunications, an area that is increasingly central in both research and practice. Therefore, we are looking for a candidate who:

• Has a master’s degree in Transport Engineering, Computer Science, Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, AI, statistics or related fields. It must be a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree. 
• Demonstrates strong analytical and research skills, including experience with operations research, transport modelling, and data analytics.
• Has an interest in the interaction between technology, transport, and public policy.
• Possesses strong communication skills in spoken and written English and enjoys working in international and interdisciplinary environments.
• Is proactive, collaborative, and motivated to engage with academic, public-sector, and industry partners.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education.

Assessment
The assessment of the candidates will be made by the supervisory committee, which consists of Associate Professor Guido Cantelmo (main supervisor) and Professor Otto Anker Nielsen, DTU Management, and Associate Professor Lucas Bréhon-Grataloup (co-supervisor), Télécom SudParis, Institut Polytechnique de Paris.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data for mapping submerged landscapes and archaeological potential
jobs.description:
The Department of Geoscience, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data, with the aim of identifying submerged landscapes and locations of archaeological potential. We are searching for a motivated and engaged researcher with experience in inversion to be part of our research team studying late Quaternary and Holocene processes and landscape evolution.

The postdoctoral position is a fixed-term full-time position for 1 year.

The postdoctoral work will be part of the international ERC Synergy Grant project SUBNORDICA, where scientists in the fields of geology, geophysics, and archaeology work together to develop methodologies for recreating submerged landscapes and human settlement in NW Europe, and for finding submerged Stone Age settlements in deeper water settings such as the North Sea. SUBNORDICA also uses machine-learning routines to identify, from existing and new data, targets of archaeological potential for more detailed investigation. The research team at the department is leading a work package focused on the eastern North Sea region. Other members in the team work on geophysical imaging methods, sea level modelling, and palaeolandscape mapping to generate palaeotopography and palaeocoastlines using both legacy and newly acquired data.

Job description
The postdoctoral position is focused on probabilistic inversion of seismic data to estimate subsurface properties that can be linked directly to the location of submerged settlements – a key example being the presence of peat, which marks former dry land.

Specific tasks will be to:

• Develop probabilistic inversion workflows for high-resolution subbottom profiles and multichannel seismic data from the North Sea, constrained by sediment core observations
• Map peat and other landscape types relevant for archaeology, and use the results together with machine-learning routines to identify targets of archaeological potential
• Provide input and constraints for predictive modelling workflows carried out at partner institutions
The postdoctoral researcher will be working closely together with post docs and senior staff in the research team at the department, as well as with the international partners in the SUBNORDICA project. Close collaboration is expected particularly with partners focused on predictive modelling for archaeology. The position provides opportunities for offshore field work and participation in joint research expeditions in the North Sea and Baltic Sea. It is also expected that the postdoc will take an active part in various research team activities and contribute to supervision and teaching of (under-) graduate students in the team.

Facilities
Laboratory facilities at the Department of Geoscience will be available for the position. This includes the acquisition, processing and interpretation facilities at SeisLab Aarhus for both multi- and single channel marine seismic and acoustic data, and an advanced sediment core laboratory.

Qualifications
The qualified applicant will have a PhD degree in geoscience, geophysics or related fields. Candidates should preferably have a background within probabilistic inversion and uncertainty quantification and/or machine learning. Experience with seismic data, including reflection seismic and hydroacoustic data, is beneficial, as is experience with linking seismic data to physical or lithological properties. Experience with the shallow subsurface of the North Sea or other similar settings, including sediment cores and marine geoarchaeology, is further beneficial but not required.

The candidate is expected to have well-documented research experience with academic publications and presentations at conferences and meetings. The applicant should also have effective organizational skills, with previous project management being beneficial. The candidate should be able to work collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team of geophysicists, geologists and archaeologists. Oral and written English skills are required.

Application
The application must include the following:

• Cover Letter, including motivation for applying and information on how the candidate’s qualifications and experience will aid the project
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications
• PhD certificate or a statement regarding the expected date of completing of PhD studies

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Statistical learning as a tool to understand host-microbiome-flavour interactions in plant growth
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a two-year position at the University of Copenhagen, as part of the ongoing Novo Nordisk Foundation funded project ‘Tomatoponics’. The goal of the project is to apply statistical and machine learning tools to multi-omics data including plant genotypes, root microbiomes and fruit shotgun metabolomes to better understand how the host and microbiome affect the fruit flavour. We aim to go beyond genotype-phenotype associations to reveal causal pathways, that will be tested in future trials.

  The candidate will be principally advised by Assoc. Prof. Shyam Gopalakrishnan, who leads the FindingPheno project based at the Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics (https://ceh.ku.dk), with additional guidance from Prof Tom Gilbert, Director of the Center. The Gopalakrishnan research group focuses on using population and statistical genetics to understand genotype-phenotype associations with a special focus on the role of microbiomes in evolutionary processes.

  Information on the department can be found at https://globe.ku.dk.

  Your job

  You will analyse a pre-generated dataset consisting of root metagenomes, resequenced plant genomes, untargeted fruit metabolomes plus other phenotypic data from a dataset of 10 cultivars exposed to 4 different microbiome treatments. The first part of the project will focus on performing exploratory analyses to understand the relationship between host genomic processes and microbiome variations that have a significant impact on the plant fruit chemistry and other phenotypes, with a particular focus on host-microbiome interactions. Subsequently, statistical and machine learning models will be applied to better understand the biological mechanisms and pathways involved, to help design a second trial aimed at testing predictions generated from the data.

  Our research

  As part of the projects, the postdoctoral fellow will collaborate with the wider team, that additionally includes researchers at the Department of Food Science (UCPH), Aarhus University and Aalborg University. The candidate will also have an opportunity to interact with the tomato industry, such as Danish based growers. Thus, teamwork and collaboration will be important skills; however, the candidate will also be given ownership over their own research project and deliverables.

  The fully funded postdoctoral fellowship will be hosted at the Section for Hologenomics/Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics at the GLOBE Institute. As such the candidate will also have the opportunity to collaborate with leaders in the fields of world leading experts in population genetics, statistical genetics, computational biology, clinical microbiology, archaeology, evolutionary genomics, and many other related fields of research. The University of Copenhagen is a world-leading institution of higher learning and provides excellent programs in genetics, archaeology, statistics, computer science and mathematics.

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• PhD degree or equivalent doctorate, with a background in one or more of the following areas: statistics, data science, statistical genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, and/or mathematics 	
• Demonstrated working proficiency in one or more programming languages commonly used in data science (e.g. Python, R, C/C++, Java or Julia) 	
• Experience working in the UNIX operating environment 	
• Excellent English skills written and spoken   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Previous experience or strong interest in working with large scale biological data such as genomics, metagenomics, multi-omics, etc. 	
• Experience with high-performance computing clusters/systems 	
• Experience with compiling and working with data from different sources 	
• Understanding of FAIR data principles, interest in Open Data 	
• Interest in scientific communication and/or public outreach   Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Section for Hologenomics, Oester Farimagsgade 5, 1353 Copenhagen C.

  About Globe Institute
 The Globe Institute is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen. The Institute’s main purpose is to address basic scientific questions through interdisciplinary approaches. The institute operates at the intersection of natural and medical sciences and the humanities. Information on the institute can be found at: http://www.globe.ku.dk/.

  The Globe Institute is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where employees and students can belong and thrive. See website for more information. All qualified applicants will receive full consideration. Candidates who, through their research, teaching, and/or service, contribute to diversity and competencies of our Institute are encouraged to apply. The University of Copenhagen strives to offer a family friendly and flexible working environment with a sustainable balance between work- and private life, including parental leave schemes (up to 47 weeks for both parents) and up to six weeks of paid holidays per year. Researchers that have not been tax liable in Denmark for the last 10 years can apply for a special (reduced) tax scheme. The university offers a variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families.

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The psoition is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is on 1st of April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Questions
 For further information please contact Assoc. Prof. Shyam Gopalakrishnan: shyam.gopalakrishnan@sund.ku.dk  and/or Prof. Tom Gilbert: tgilbert@sund.ku.dk .

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position.

• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 17 January 2027, 23.59pm CET.

 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
